I’ve been hella bummed about not being able to do my usual weekly UNCUT entries because I just don’t have the mental capacity for them at the moment. (It’s been about three months since my last recording.) Even when it comes to physically building products for PoG, I haven’t been able to do much lately.

My energy has been going into job hunting—trying to land a corporate 9–5 role to bring some financial stability back into my life. The last time I worked in corporate was in 2020. Since then, it’s been freelancing and odd jobs here and there. Right now, I’m working part-time at Everyman Cinema to make ends meet.

But yeah… building a fashion brand ain’t sexy. Building a business ain’t sexy either, for that matter.

Can’t be a starving artist with a mind full of gold. Sometimes you’ve got to play the game of life.

I guess the new format of UNCUT will be these snapshots of whatever phase of life I’m currently in.

Building @pioneersofgreatness

What do you do when life hits you from all angles? When shit ain’t going your way? 

You ride that shit out.

This ain’t a sprint. It’s a marathon.

A 12-round fight… Fuck it. A 15-rounder.

Stay in the fight long enough to see the results. Long enough to outlast the bullshit life throws at you.

When I’m not building PoG, I’m building the mind and body capable of building it.

Much needed reset.

Only been to a handful of chill hikes like Bamford Edge, Rivelin Valley, and Arthur’s Seat, which were all under 300m of a climb. But nothing compared to hiking the base of the Matterhorn in Cervinia (more or less a 1,000m climb at just under 3,000m altitude). Despite being the slowest in the group, not bad for someone with a torn ACL (didn’t even buckle once) and hiking in AF1s!

Experiences like this remind me how much of what goes on in our day-to-day lives doesn’t even matter. But you gotta play the game. Once I’m UP, I’m defo gonna disappear off into nature and live the rest of my life painting. Until then, I got a brand to build…

To me, great designers don’t just build great products. They build a language so they can write poetry.

That’s how I’m approaching the development of PoG.

I’m creating a design language that doesn’t rely on logos, but instead on form, function, construction, materiality, scale, abstraction, and subtraction. The goal is for every product to speak the same language, regardless of category, material, or silhouette.

There’s no expiration date on ideas. Execute in da long run.

Proud of this one. First ever trousers I’ve designed from start to finish. From ideation, pattern drafting/cutting, prototyping, through to sampling.

But the job’s not done. I’ve only made two samples so far (one back in November 2025 and this one), as well as four prototypes.

So there’s still further refinement to be done:

* slight tightness around the crotch area
* fabric pooling beneath the glutes
* further construction issues to resolve

…But overall, the fit is there.

Can’t emphasise enough how important it is to execute an idea and improve it later. And this right here is a testament to that.

Back then, the best way I could bring an idea to life was through sketching, so that’s exactly what I did.

This was also a custom made to order for my good friend and he hand picked the denim himself so it’s a lighter denim (10z instead of the usual 14oz with a bleached wash) and he also wanted the collar to be shortened.

Mistakes are part of the process.

Yesterday I was ready to screenprint “PIONEERS OF GREATNESS” under the back yolk—but because I dyed the fabric the night before, I didn’t account for shrinkage. The jacket shrunk a fair bit. Luckily it started oversized, so now it’s closer to true-to-size. Not what I planned, but it is what it is.

The issue is the graphic no longer sits flush under the arched yolk—the whole reason I designed it that way. That arch detail goes back to 2023, when I first embroidered the brand name on a Levi’s Trucker. Back then, I didn’t have the skills to build a jacket from scratch, so I made it work on an existing one. Now, I can.

Plenty more mistakes were made (you’ll see in the clips), but still… not bad for my first denim jacket sewn from scratch and dyed in-house. I’ll give myself some grace.

Now it’s about making sure sample no.2 is on point.

Fast fashion has created an illusion that creating garments is a cheap process but the reality of it is a lot of craftsmanship goes into developing a product before it ends up in your wardrobe.

6 months hiatus with @pioneersofgreatness but working behind the scenes.

I’ve been in the studio, sharpening my skills under @robertjesse_ and learning the craft from the ground up.

Now it’s time to apply it to P°G!

The P°G Training Knit Vest has been my go to for boxing sessions these past few months: tested, worn, pushed. I know what needs to evolve and what needs to stay.

Pattern Drafting. 
Cutting. 
Sewing. 
Prototyping.
Brick by brick. 
Product by product.

Time to lock in! 🎯

Coming up 6 months shadowing @robertjesse_ 

I’ve learnt a handful of sewing techniques and industry insights. Got my hands dirty with pattern making, pattern drafting and sewing dope pieces from client work such as a jacket that turns into a bag, a hoodie sample for Samuel Ross, plus bag development and the Rain Cycle Jacket for @prsnl.hb 

Being able to use industrial machines that are way more powerful than the home machines I’ve used—just in the thick of it learning the craft from the bottom up. Made a lot of mistakes and learnt from them—the best teacher is hands on experience. Can’t learn this from a textbook, you gotta do the damn thing!

We stay learning, student of the game—learning from the best! 📚
